recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Reintroducing the older prior-to-commencement wording would conflict with the accepted FHIR-10416 definition and current Task guidance that cancellation can occur from non-terminal states.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Task issue FHIR-10416 requested adding a cancelled TaskStatus code because Task cancellation behavior was already implied by the Task cancel operation and request/order lifecycle. The accepted resolution was to add cancelled as a status with the meaning that the task was not completed as requested.
initial_application: The status code was added in the DSTU2-era workflow changes, and commit 135effcdc18c5860253e8fc6df7197732441fe74 explicitly tagged #10416 while revising the cancelled definition from the earlier withdrawn-prior-to-commencement wording to 'the task was not completed (more or less) as requested.' Current source is the post-refactor CodeSystem source, not the old spreadsheet, and it still includes cancelled in the active Task status code system.
additional_context: FHIR-11431 is the tightly related workflow clarification explaining that when the placer cancels a task, the placer is no longer concerned about the task outcome and the filler should cease work if able. Later FHIR-14781 moved and expanded the Task state-machine text into the Task page without removing the cancelled status. The active build includes task=Task, and the TaskStatus ValueSet includes the whole Task status code system. No directly relevant Zulip or Confluence record was found that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active source already contains the cancelled code in source/task/codesystem-task-status.xml, includes it through source/task/valueset-task-status.xml, and provides cancellation behavior guidance in source/task/task-notes.xml and the workflow ad-hoc page.

related_jiras.note: Clarifies the placer/filler cancellation scenario that uses the cancelled status added for this issue.
Moved Task state-machine explanatory text onto the Task page while preserving cancellation semantics.
